canonical_name: Domain Name System — RFC 1034/1035 living core

standardized.notes: RFC 1034 and RFC 1035 published as the paired DNS concepts/implementation core.

last_known_use.notes: Core namespace, delegation, server/resolver, caching and message/RR architecture remains recognizable in production DNS.

addressing: Maps hierarchical names to typed resource data; not limited to host-address records.
routing_or_forwarding: Delegation and iterative/recursive resolution guide queries across authoritative boundaries; DNS is not an IP routing protocol.
error_control: Application protocol response/error codes; reliability depends on selected transport and retry behavior.
flow_or_congestion_control: No independent end-to-end congestion-control algorithm; transport-dependent.

survival.provenance_notes: Reference example of a stable core architecture supporting a large forest of later extensions.

open_questions: Build RR-type genealogy from original types through AAAA, SRV, DNSSEC, CAA, SVCB/HTTPS and others.
Trace resolver and authoritative-server implementation history.
Separate core DNS semantics from later transport/privacy branches.
notes: Reference example for living-core-with-extension-forest survival: later DNS features typically extend rather than replace the RFC 1034/1035 architectural skeleton.
